newsitem.title: THAILAND: HSBC Investment Bank Asia bullish on Thailand.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Investment Bank Asia bullish on Thailand.

text.p: HSBC Investment Bank Asia Ltd said on Tuesday it and other units in the HSBC Group Plc remained positive about medium term prospects of the Thai economy despite a recent decision by Moody's Investors Service to downgrade Thailand's short-term debt rating.

HSBC Investment Bank's chairman Paul Selway-Swift said bankers do not all share Moody's view about Thailand and he expected any impact from a lower Thai rating, in raising financing costs of Thai corporate borrowers, to be only temporary and minimal.

Moody's last month downgraded Thailand's short-term sovereign ceiling rating to Prime-2 from Prime-1, saying a rapid build-up of its short-term debts early this year exposed the country to financial shocks in the balance of payments.

"I don't think people are put off because of a sudden downturn of the Thai economy...some may see it as a type of opportunies. Generally people taking a medium term view on Thailand remain reasonally positive," he said.
Selway-Swift was in Thailand to launch his company's Bangkok representative office.
A banker in the HSBC Group said the Moody's decision would probably raise the average financing cost faced by small Thai companies by up to 12.5 basis points while big Thai banks remain unaffected.

"Foreign views on Thailand are very dynamic and they could turn positive any time, say by changing politics here," he said, referring to a snap election called by Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa last Friday which has been welcomed by the business community.
Christopher Weir, chief of HSBC Investment Bank's Bangkok office, said his office would focus on helping Thai clients market their equity and equity-linked products abroad.
